bull_bear.body: Prioritizing capex for manufacturing and new modalities; debt repayment completed (INR720cr via IPO); future capex funded via internal accruals and debt; no dividends or buybacks mentioned
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Biotech funding volatility; macro uncertainty from US tariffs/MFN orders; long lead times for commercialization of pipeline molecules; execution risk on large capex projects; customer concentration risk (18 of top 25 pharma)
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, forward-looking, and execution-focused; emphasized supply chain shift as key tailwind; highlighted customer-led innovation in new modalities; downplayed near-term macro noise; reiterated long-term guidance firmly
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The INR34cr Q4 provision was a one-time de-stocking issue with a customer, not systemic credit risk; 37% of CRO revenue now from pharma (not biotech), indicating structural shift; Boston center is EBITDA profitable and contributes $14-15M revenue; capex is largely for FY27 delivery, not FY26
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- CFO cites "a healthy balance sheet and disciplined capital allocation" as underpinning confidence in executing the long-term growth strategy.
- Spending is directed at capacity and capability rather than returns to shareholders — Rs 263 Cr capex in the quarter against a 65% utilised 700 KL base, plus a doubled PRD block, a Bidar expansion and land banked at Choutuppal.
- Management reiterates long-term revenue growth guidance of 15-20% and an EBITDA range of 28-30%.
- The deck makes no mention of dividend, buyback, debt levels or net cash.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: CDMO: 63% of revenue; CRO: 37% of revenue; CRO growth driven by pharma clients (now 37-38% of CRO revenue vs 30% last year); discovery chemistry: 60% of CRO; biology/DMPK: 40%; peptide center launched in Hyderabad; new modalities (ADC, oligo) capex underway

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Founded in 1999 and described as having "transformed into an integrated CRDMO, delivering value across the pharma lifecycle from early discovery to commercial manufacturing"; operates as both a CRO and a CDMO offering an end-to-end platform.
- Trusted by 300+ global clients including 19 of the top 25 global pharma companies (footnoted as "In terms of market cap for CY 2025") across the US, UK, EU and Japan; average tenure of large pharma relationships is 11+ years.
- Claims to be the fastest growing Indian CRDMO over the last 5 years, with 26% revenue CAGR over that period and a 100% successful track record of regulatory inspections across R&D and manufacturing facilities (USFDA, PMDA).
- Track record cited: 5 molecules taken from discovery to market, 50+ programs advanced to candidate nomination/IND or Phase I/II/III, across oncology, CNS, metabolic diseases, inflammation, antivirals, rare diseases and more.
- MD & CEO frames the moat as a shift in customer demand: large pharma now wants "strong, scientifically led partners who can take greater ownership of integrated discovery and development programs, rather than simply execute individual pieces of work".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Listing] Listed on the Indian stock exchanges (NSE/BSE) in December 2024; NSE symbol SaiLife, BSE code 544306.
- [Partnership] Strategic partnership with Schrodinger to enhance discovery science (2019-2023 phase of the growth journey).
- [Customer engagement model] Expanded a top-tier pharma relationship into an end-to-end collaboration spanning discovery to commercial; FTE engagements are beginning to contribute late-phase assets, and the CEO expects strategic engagements to "create a healthy and sustained pipeline over multiple years".
- [Revenue visibility] Deck states "Over 90% Pipeline Visibility on FY27 Targets".
- [Client stickiness] More than 65% of Discovery revenues in FY23-26 came from customers who availed more than one Discovery service (chemistry, biology and/or DMPK).

deepdive.thesis: Sai Life Sciences is a leading integrated CRDMO in India benefiting from global pharma's supply chain diversification away from China, with strong execution in discovery, development, and manufacturing. Its strategic capex expansion in peptides, ADCs, and oligonucleotides positions it to capture high-growth next-gen therapeutics demand while improving margins toward 28-30%.
